Categories.value: Kiscell Museum|Self-published work|1856 statues in Hungary|Statues in Budapest District III|Statues of dragons in Hungary|Relocated sculptures in Hungary|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Iron statues in Hungary|June 2025 in Budapest

ImageDescription.value: Statue of a Dragon by Frigyes Feszl. First installed at the Chain Bridge quay/ship loading area/ in 1856. Relocated to current place in/before 1944 (other source after 1945). At the southern entrance of the quay storage stood gate sculptures shaped like dolphins, while on the northern side were three dragons (were they intended as icebreakers in case of spring floods?). Based on a 1953 photo two dragon statues can be see before the Museum, however since 1970s only one dragon is here - 108 Kiscelli Street, Doberdó Road, Óbuda hegyvidéke neighbourhood,3rd district of Budapest.

ImageDescription.value: Former Schmidt Mansion complex, northwest part. Former Trinitarian church wing? or connecting part??. The upper layer of the Kiscell plateau is made up of loess sediment, which was an excellent soil for viticulture. - The memory of wine production is represented by the rock cellar under the Kiscelli Museum, a natural cavity expanded into a 400 m2 cave; it was the wine cellar of the Trinitarian monks, and after the dissolution of the order, it served as a food storage for the stationed army. - Kiscelli Street,Óbuda hegyvidéke neighbourhood,3rd district of Budapest.

ImageDescription.value: Former Schmidt Mansion complex, northwest part. Former Trinitarian church wing. It has barred cellar windows. The upper layer of the Kiscell plateau is made up of loess sediment, which was an excellent soil for grape growing. - The memory of wine production is represented by the rock cellar under the Kiscelli Museum, a natural cavity expanded into a 400 m2 cave; it was the wine cellar of the Trinitarian monks, and after the dissolution of the order (end of the 18th century), it served as a food storage for the military that settled there (till end of the 19th century). - Kiscelli Street, Óbuda hegyvidéke neighbourhood,3rd district of Budapest.

ImageDescription.value: Lapidary? before the former Trinitarian church wing of the former Schmidt Mansion complex, northeast part. The obelisk inscribed with "Free Buda, capital city on May 23, 1844 // 323 Budapest capital city 1882". It is likely that it was a border stone of Buda when it was erected in 1844, and from 1882 onwards, it served as the border stone number 323 of Budapest. - Kiscelli Street, Óbuda hegyvidéke neighbourhood,3rd district of Budapest.
